status.text: The Senate voted 73-25 to invoke cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R. 2347, the Senate floor vehicle for the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act.
status.quote: The Senate voted 73-25 on Monday, November 9, 2026, to invoke cloture on the motion to proceed

items.outlet: Clean Energy and business coalition letter (C2ES listed as host)
items.author: Undersigned organisations (86 counted)
items.title: Sign-on Letter: Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (Senate Committee Leadership)
items.summary: Eighty-six organisations signed a letter to the four committee leaders urging passage of the bill. The letter is dated November 9, 2026, and does not mention the November 7 substitute. Signers in the list include the National Association of Manufacturers, Chamber of Progress, Third Way, Evergreen Action, Citizens' Climate Lobby and ClearPath Action; the count is mine, from the extracted signature block.

quote.text: We encourage passage of this bipartisan legislation that represents a crucial step toward improving permitting and review processes
quote.speaker: The undersigned organisations, to Chair Capito, Chair Lee, Ranking Member Whitehouse and Ranking Member Heinrich

letter.to: Chair Shelley Moore Capito; Chair Mike Lee; Ranking Member Sheldon Whitehouse; Ranking Member Martin Heinrich
letter.ask: Encourages passage of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026.

items.author: U.S. Chamber of Commerce and coalition signers
items.title: Coalition letter: Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (PDF; page lists it as published November 6, 2026)
items.summary: The Chamber and its coalition urged Congress to pass the bill, which the letter identifies as S. 5653. The letter is dated November 6, 2026, before the November 7 substitute. The document states no signer count; the count of about 521 is my tally of the signature block (Chamber, national organisations and state and local chambers), so treat it as approximate.

quote.text: we urge Congress to pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, historic comprehensive permitting reform legislation, and send it to the President's desk as soon as possible
quote.speaker: U.S. Chamber of Commerce, on behalf of the undersigned organizations

letter.to: To the Members of the United States Congress
letter.ask: Pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 and send it to the President's desk as soon as possible.

items.title: Leadership Stakeholder Letter on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (PDF)
items.summary: A letter dated October 21, 2026 to Thune, Johnson, Schumer and Jeffries urged floor action on S. 5653 this year. It is not in the tracker; the date is before the window and is included because the document is not held. Signer count is my count of the signature block, about 137 lines, and may include wrapped lines.

quote.text: we urge you to bring the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (S. 5653) to the floor and deliver much-needed permitting reform for American consumers this year
quote.speaker: Undersigned organisations (lead: American Petroleum Institute)

letter.to: Majority Leader John Thune; Speaker Mike Johnson; Minority Leader Charles Schumer; Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries
letter.ask: Bring S. 5653 to the floor and deliver permitting reform this year.

events.title: Senate cloture vote on the motion to proceed to H.R. 2347
events.summary: The Senate voted 73-25 to invoke cloture on the motion to proceed to H.R. 2347, the vehicle for the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act. The vote was procedural, not final passage.
